# Reading and preparing the data

```{r}
obs_data <- read.csv("obs_data.csv")
seg_data <- read.csv("seg_data.csv")
obs_data$dist <- (obs_data$distbegin + obs_data$distend) / 2
obs_data$region <- factor(ifelse(obs_data$lat < 39, "South", "North"), levels = c("South", "North"))
# Add the temperature of the corresponding segment to each sighting.
segment_match <- match(obs_data$Sample.Label, seg_data$Sample.Label)
obs_data$SST_day <- seg_data$SST_day[segment_match]
# A segment may contain more than one sighting. For the first analysis,
# retain only one row per segment in which dolphins were detected.
detection_segments <- obs_data[!duplicated(obs_data$Sample.Label), ]

```


Confirm the dimensions of the objects and the number of missing values in the variables you will analyse.

```{r}
# Complete and run.
dim(obs_data)
# 737 linhas e 18 colunas
```


# Exercise 1 Before testing

## 1. the ecological question

Se os golfinhos se econtram em alguma temperatura específica, foi visto que apareciam em locais em que a temperatura era menor que 20ºC\
OU\
Might our sample of observations be consistent with dolphins preferring tempertures below 20ºC? 


## 2. the sampling unit (unidade de amostragem)

The sampling units are segments of effort with dolphins detected on them. We have `r dim(detection_segments)[1]` of these.\
OU
```{r}
nrow(detection_segments)
```


## 3. the response variable and its measurement scale (variável de resposta)
A temperatura\
The temperature, and it is a continuous variable


## 4. The null hypothesis $H_0$ and alternative $H_1$, using symbols and words
hipotese nula é menor ou igual a 20ºC
hipotese alternativa é maior ou igual a 20ºC

$H_0: \mu \le 20$ \

the mean value of segments where dolphins exist is less or equal to 20\

$H_1: \mu > 20$
 

## 5. the significance level
alfa = 0.01\
I will choose 0.01, i only want to find a non existing effect 1 out of every 100 times i would conduct the test.


## 6. the relevant assumptions

The assumptions (of a parametric teste over the mean) are:\
1. the observations should be independent\

2. the residuals (here it is the same as the observations) should be Gaussian

# Exercise 2 One-sample test

## Question
In segments containing at least one detection, is the mean sea-surface temperature compatible with 20 °C?\

Use a two-sided test with (H_0: = 20) °C. This question describes conditions in segments with detections. On its own, it is not a test of habitat preference because it does not compare segments with and without detections.\

## 4.2 Exploration and assumptions\

**1. Calculate (n), the mean, median, standard deviation and standard error.**\


```{r}
hist(detection_segments$SST_day, main="", xlab="Temperature (ºC)")
abline(v=20,lty=2,lwd=3,col="lightblue")
abline(v=mean(detection_segments$SST_day),lty=2,lwd=3,col="red")
legend("topleft", lty=c(2,1), lwd=3, col=c("lightblue","red"), legend=c("H0","Observed mean"))
```


```{r}
mean(detection_segments$SST_day)
sd(detection_segments$SST_day)
range(detection_segments$SST_day)
```

The minimum value of SST where a dolphin was observed was `r round(min(detection_segments$SST_day),2)`
the maximum was `r max(detection_segments$SST_day)` and the mean was `r mean(detection_segments$SST_day)` ºC.

**2. Evaluate the assumptions of a parametric test for the mean**\

i will use a kolmogrov-smirnov test for gaussanity. first need to standardize the data
```{r}
#standardizar os dados
#subtrair a media e dividir pelo desvio padrao
scaledSST <- detection_segments$SST_day - mean(detection_segments$SST_day)/sd(detection_segments$SST_day)
ks.test(scaledSST, y="pnorm")
```


Given the p value, i should reject H0. that means that strictly i should use a non-parametric test.

Teste nao paramétrico

```{r}
wilcox.test(x=detection_segments$SST_day, mu=20, alternative ="two.sided")
```

But this was a bilateral test, but we want a unilateral test - remember our $H0$

```{r}
wilcox.test(x=detection_segments$SST_day, mu=20, alternative ="greater")

```

### **4.3 The t-test and confidence interval** 
run the test and identify the estimate, t estatistic, degrees of freedom, p-value and 95% confidence interval\

implementei um teste de t, even if the assumption test tells me i should not
```{r}
myttestBi <- t.test(x=detection_segments$SST_day , mu =20, alternative = "two.sided",)
names(myttestBi)
myttestBi$conf.int
```


```{r}
t.test(x=detection_segments$SST_day , mu=20, alternative = "greater",)

```



**Explain why the confidence interval and the two-sided test lead to the same decision about 20°C.**

```{r}
hist(detection_segments$SST_day, main="", xlab="Temperature (ºC)")
abline(v=20,lty=2,lwd=3,col="lightblue")
abline(v=mean(detection_segments$SST_day),lty=2,lwd=3,col="red")
legend("topleft", lty=c(1,1), lwd=3, col=c("lightblue","red","darkgreen"), legend=c("H0","Observed mean","95% CI"))

abline(v=myttestBi$conf.int,lty=2, col="darkgreen",lwd=3)
```

## 5 Exercise 3 Two independent samples

Does the mean size of observed groups differ north and south of 39° N?\
1. Write (H_0) and (H_1).\
2. Show the number of sightings in each region.\
3. Calculate the mean, median and standard deviation for each region.\
4. Visualise the distributions on the original scale and after applying log1p(size).\


```{r}
table(obs_data$region)
```

We have `r sum(obs_data$region=="South")` observations in the south and `r sum(obs_data$region=="North")` in the north.


```{r}
mytab <- rbind(tapply(X=obs_data$size, INDEX = obs_data$region, FUN=mean), tapply(X=obs_data$size, INDEX = obs_data$region, FUN=median), tapply(X=obs_data$size, INDEX = obs_data$region, FUN=sd))
row.names(mytab) <- c("Mean","Median","Standard Deviation")
knitr::kable(mytab)

```

```{r}
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
boxplot(obs_data$size ~ obs_data$region, data = obs_data)
boxplot(log1p(obs_data$size) ~ obs_data$region, data = obs_data)

```



Testar usando o teste de t

```{r}
t.test(x=obs_data$size[obs_data$region=="South"],y= obs_data$size[obs_data$region=="North"],alternative ="two.sided")
```

Testar usando o teste de wilcox, nível de significancia 0.01
```{r}
wilcox.test(x=obs_data$size[obs_data$region=="South"],y= obs_data$size[obs_data$region=="North"],alternative ="two.sided")

```
